title: Psalms Chapter 146 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 146 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 146 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 146.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's command in Psalms 146:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:1 commands to praise the LORD: "Praise ye the LORD. Praise the LORD, O my soul."

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:2, how long will the psalmist praise the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:2 says, "While I live will I praise the LORD: I will sing praises unto my God while I have any being."

questions.question: In Psalms 146:3, in whom should you NOT put your trust?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 advises, "Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help."

questions.question: What happens to a man’s thoughts when his breath goes forth, according to Psalms 146:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:4 states, "His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146:1 commands the soul to praise the LORD.
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:1 says, "Praise ye the LORD. Praise the LORD, O my soul." This shows the soul is commanded to praise the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146:3 encourages us to trust in princes for help.
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 says, "Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help." It explicitly forbids trusting in princes.

questions.question: What does Psalms 146:2 say the psalmist will do while he has any being?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:2 states, "I will sing praises unto my God while I have any being."

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:4, when does a man return to his earth?
options: At the end of the year
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:4 says, "His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish."

questions.question: Who is described as having no help in Psalms 146:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 states, "Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146:2 says the psalmist will praise the LORD only when he is young.
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:2 says, "While I live will I praise the LORD: I will sing praises unto my God while I have any being." It does not restrict praise to youth.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's soul told to do in Psalms 146:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:1 says, "Praise ye the LORD. Praise the LORD, O my soul." The soul is commanded to praise the LORD.

questions.question: In Psalms 146:4, what is said to perish on the same day a man dies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:4 says, "in that very day his thoughts perish."

questions.question: Which comes first in Psalms 146:1-4?
options: Put not your trust in princes
While I live will I praise the LORD
questions.explanation: The first instruction in Psalms 146 is to "Praise ye the LORD" (verse 1), before the other statements in verses 2-4.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146:4 says a man's breath goeth forth and he returns to the earth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:4 clearly states, "His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth."

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:3, what is the source of no help?
options: Princes and the son of man
questions.correctAnswer: Princes and the son of man
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 says, "Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help."

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 146 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 146 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:5, what is the source of true happiness?
options: Having the God of Jacob for help
Being wise in one's own eyes
questions.correctAnswer: Having the God of Jacob for help
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:5 states that happy is he who has the God of Jacob as his help and whose hope is in the LORD his God, indicating true happiness comes from trusting God, not worldly powers.

questions.question: What does Psalms 146:6 say about God's role in creation and His faithfulness?
options: He made only the heavens and is sometimes truthful
He created everything and keeps truth forever
He made the sea but forgets the earth
questions.correctAnswer: He created everything and keeps truth forever
questions.explanation: Verse 6 emphasizes God's creation of heaven, earth, sea, and all within, and His eternal faithfulness in keeping truth forever.

questions.question: Which actions of the LORD are listed in Psalms 146:7?
options: He giveth food to the proud and looseth kings
He executeth judgment for the oppressed and giveth food to the hungry
He openeth the eyes of the wise and raiseth the mighty
He blesseth the wicked and forsaketh the poor
questions.correctAnswer: He executeth judgment for the oppressed and giveth food to the hungry
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:7 describes the LORD as executing judgment for the oppressed, giving food to the hungry, and loosening prisoners, highlighting His care for those in need.

questions.question: How does Psalms 146:8 describe the LORD's care for people with physical and emotional burdens?
options: He ignores the blind but blesses the strong
He openeth the eyes of the blind and raiseth those bowed down
He only helps the righteous and leaves others alone
He strengthens the proud and weakens the humble
questions.correctAnswer: He openeth the eyes of the blind and raiseth those bowed down
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows God's compassion by opening the eyes of the blind and raising those who are bowed down, demonstrating His care for both physical and emotional burdens.

questions.question: What does Psalms 146:9 say about God's protection and justice?
options: God only cares for the wealthy
God preserves strangers and relieves the fatherless and widow
God ignores the widow and punishes the righteous
God favors the wicked over the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves strangers and relieves the fatherless and widow
questions.explanation: Verse 9 highlights God's preservation of strangers and relief to the fatherless and widow, while turning the way of the wicked upside down, demonstrating His justice and care.

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:10, what is the duration of the LORD's reign?
options: Only during the lifetime of the righteous
questions.explanation: Verse 10 declares the LORD shall reign forever, even to all generations, emphasizing the eternal nature of God's sovereignty.

questions.question: Psalms 146:5 says 'Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help.' How does this verse connect to the description of God in the next verse (146:6)?
options: Because God is an earthly king, he helps only some
Because God made all creation and keeps truth forever, He is trustworthy help
Because God is far away, help is uncertain
Because God is silent, help must be sought elsewhere
questions.correctAnswer: Because God made all creation and keeps truth forever, He is trustworthy help
questions.explanation: Verse 6 supports verse 5 by showing that God's role as Creator and keeper of truth makes Him a trustworthy source of help and hope.

questions.question: What promise in Psalms 146:7 follows from the hope described in Psalms 146:5?
options: God will punish those who trust Him
God executes judgment for the oppressed and provides food for the hungry
God ignores those who hope in Him
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment for the oppressed and provides food for the hungry
questions.explanation: Since verse 5 calls those happy who hope in the LORD, verse 7 shows how God acts on behalf of the oppressed and hungry, confirming the blessings of trusting Him.

questions.question: How does Psalms 146:8 build on the actions described in Psalms 146:7 to demonstrate God's character?
options: God only judges but does not help
God actively opens eyes, raises the bowed down, and loves the righteous, showing His loving care
God punishes those who are blind
questions.correctAnswer: God actively opens eyes, raises the bowed down, and loves the righteous, showing His loving care
questions.explanation: Verse 8 extends verse 7's themes by showing God not only judges and feeds but also heals and uplifts, revealing His comprehensive love and care.

questions.question: A believer is struggling with feelings of helplessness and oppression. Based on Psalms 146, what biblical truth should encourage them?
options: They should put their trust in princes for help
God executes judgment for the oppressed and gives food to the hungry
Their struggles are ignored by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment for the oppressed and gives food to the hungry
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:7 assures that God actively judges oppression and provides for those in need, offering hope and encouragement to the struggling believer.

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:5-8, which of the following best illustrates how faith in God impacts a believer's life?
options: Faith leads to reliance on human leaders
Faith results in hope and experiencing God's help and care
Faith is based on material wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Faith results in hope and experiencing God's help and care
questions.explanation: Verses 5-8 present the blessedness of trusting God, who provides help, judgment, sustenance, healing, and love, showing faith leads to hope and divine care.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146:6 teaches that God only made the heavens and earth but does not keep truth forever.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 explicitly says God made the heavens, earth, sea, and all therein, and that He keeps truth forever, showing both creation and eternal faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 146:9, the LORD relieves the fatherless and widow and preserves strangers.
questions.explanation: Verse 9 clearly states that the LORD preserves strangers and relieves the fatherless and widow, highlighting His protective care.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146:3 warns to put your trust in princes because they provide help.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 warns against trusting princes or sons of men because in them there is no help, encouraging trust in God instead.

questions.question: How does Psalms 146 teach believers about humility and dependence on God rather than human power?
options: By urging trust in princes and kings
By warning not to put trust in man who perishes, but to hope in God who reigns forever
questions.correctAnswer: By warning not to put trust in man who perishes, but to hope in God who reigns forever
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 and 10 contrast the frailty of humans with God's eternal reign, teaching humility and dependence on God rather than on human power.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 146 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 146.

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:9, whom does the LORD preserve and relieve?
options: The strangers, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.correctAnswer: The strangers, the fatherless, and the widow
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:9 states that the LORD preserves the strangers and relieves the fatherless and widow, highlighting God's care for vulnerable groups.

questions.question: What does Psalms 146:9 say happens to the way of the wicked?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the way of the wicked he turneth upside down, indicating divine judgment against evil.

questions.question: Psalms 146:10 declares the LORD shall reign forever. To whom is this reign specifically addressed?
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that the LORD shall reign forever, even thy God, O Zion, emphasizing God's eternal kingship over Zion.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage closely parallels the theme of God's care for the oppressed found in Psalms 146:7-9?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:17 exhorts to seek justice, relieve the oppressed, and defend the fatherless, echoing Psalms 146's themes of divine justice and care.

questions.question: What is the literary device used in Psalms 146:1-2 where the psalmist calls upon his soul to praise the LORD and commits to praising while alive?
questions.explanation: The verses show synonymous parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, repeating the theme of praise with different expressions.

questions.question: The phrase 'Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man' from Psalms 146:3 is an example of what kind of biblical teaching?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 cautions against trusting human leaders who cannot ultimately help, urging trust in God alone.

questions.question: How does Psalms 146:6 describe God's creation?
options: He made heaven, earth, sea, and all therein
He made the sun and moon
questions.correctAnswer: He made heaven, earth, sea, and all therein
questions.explanation: This verse emphasizes God's sovereignty as Creator of all things, reinforcing His eternal truthkeeping.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God opening the eyes of the blind, as mentioned in Psalms 146:8?
questions.explanation: John 9:39 records Jesus healing a man born blind, fulfilling the Old Testament theme of God opening blind eyes as in Psalms 146:8.

questions.question: In Psalms 146:7, what actions does the LORD perform for the oppressed and hungry?
questions.explanation: The verse highlights God's justice for the oppressed and provision for the hungry, demonstrating His care for the needy.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word in Psalms 146:10 is translated as 'reign,' and what is its primary meaning?
options: Malak - to reign or be king
questions.correctAnswer: Malak - to reign or be king
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'malak' means to reign or have dominion, emphasizing God's eternal kingship in Psalms 146:10.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146:4 teaches that human thoughts perish on the day a person returns to the earth.
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:4 states that when a person dies (returns to dust), their thoughts perish that very day, underscoring human mortality.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 146 encourages placing trust in earthly leaders as the ultimate source of help.
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 explicitly advises not to trust princes or the son of man, as they provide no help, emphasizing trust in God instead.

questions.question: Which other Psalm contains a similar call to praise the LORD as found in Psalms 146:1-2, forming an inclusio in the Psalter?
questions.explanation: Psalm 145 also opens with a call to praise the LORD, creating an inclusio with Psalm 146 that frames this section of the Psalter.

questions.question: In the cultural context of ancient Israel, why is the LORD's preservation of strangers, fatherless, and widows (Psalms 146:9) significant?
options: These groups were vulnerable and lacked social protection
They were the wealthiest members of society
They were priests in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: These groups were vulnerable and lacked social protection
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture, strangers, orphans, and widows had little legal or social support; God's care for them demonstrates divine justice and mercy.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of the LORD reigning forever as proclaimed in Psalms 146:10?
questions.explanation: Revelation 11:15 declares that the kingdoms of the world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and His Christ, reaffirming God's eternal reign as in Psalms 146:10.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 146 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 146 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Psalms 146:3, why should a believer not put their trust in princes or the son of man?
options: Because there is no help in them
questions.correctAnswer: Because there is no help in them
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 explicitly states that trust should not be placed in princes or the son of man because 'in whom there is no help.' This teaches the doctrine that human authority is limited and cannot ultimately save.

questions.question: What theological truth about human mortality is taught in Psalms 146:4?
options: Human breath departs and thoughts perish on the same day
Humans can save themselves through wisdom
Humans ascend to heaven after death
questions.correctAnswer: Human breath departs and thoughts perish on the same day
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:4 teaches that when a man dies, his breath goes forth, returning to the earth, and his thoughts perish that very day, underscoring the doctrine of human mortality and the transient nature of human life.

questions.question: Psalms 146:5 states 'Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help.' What doctrine does this verse primarily affirm?
options: The blessedness of trusting in God as helper
The necessity of human effort for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The blessedness of trusting in God as helper
questions.explanation: This verse affirms the doctrine of the blessedness and happiness that comes from relying on God as one's help and hope, emphasizing divine aid rather than human strength (Psalms 146:5).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 146:6 when it says God 'keepeth truth for ever'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:6 reveals God's attribute of faithfulness and unchanging truth, teaching that God preserves truth eternally, a key aspect of His nature.

questions.question: What justice-related action of God is described in Psalms 146:7?
options: God executes judgment for the oppressed and frees prisoners
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment for the oppressed and frees prisoners
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:7 describes God's justice as executing judgment for the oppressed and liberating prisoners, highlighting His role as a righteous judge and deliverer.

questions.question: Psalms 146:8 mentions several acts of God. Which attribute is most clearly demonstrated by God opening the eyes of the blind?
questions.explanation: God opening the eyes of the blind in Psalms 146:8 demonstrates His compassion and mercy toward those in need, reflecting His loving care for the vulnerable.

questions.question: Which social groups does God specifically care for according to Psalms 146:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:9 explicitly states that God preserves strangers and relieves the fatherless and widows, teaching His special concern for marginalized and vulnerable groups.

questions.question: What does Psalms 146:10 declare about the reign of the LORD?
options: The LORD's reign will end soon
The LORD shares His throne with princes
The LORD's reign is limited to the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:10 affirms the doctrine of God's eternal kingship, declaring that the LORD shall reign forever, emphasizing His sovereign and everlasting rule.

questions.question: How do Psalms 146:5-6, combined with verse 10, collectively portray God's sovereignty and character?
options: God is the eternal creator, helper, and sovereign King
God is limited to temporal power and unreliable
God depends on human princes for authority
God is distant and uninvolved in creation
questions.correctAnswer: God is the eternal creator, helper, and sovereign King
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 highlight God as helper and creator who keeps truth forever, while verse 10 emphasizes His eternal reign, collectively portraying God's sovereign, eternal kingship and faithful character.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about salvation and human trust is conveyed by comparing Psalms 146:3 and 146:5?
options: Trust in God alone, not in human rulers, is the source of true help and happiness
Human princes are the ultimate source of salvation
Trust in material wealth guarantees hope
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God alone, not in human rulers, is the source of true help and happiness
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:3 warns against trusting princes, while 146:5 affirms happiness for those trusting in God, teaching the doctrine that salvation and hope come solely from God.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine justice is a myth because the oppressed often suffer without relief. What does Psalms 146:7-9 actually teach about God's justice and care?
options: God executes judgment for the oppressed and cares for the vulnerable
God ignores the oppressed and rewards the wicked
God's justice is delayed and uncertain
God's care is limited to the righteous only
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment for the oppressed and cares for the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:7-9 teaches that God actively executes judgment for the oppressed, feeds the hungry, frees prisoners, opens the eyes of the blind, and preserves strangers, showing His just and merciful nature despite apparent earthly injustice.

questions.question: What synthesis of God's attributes is evident when considering Psalms 146:6 and 146:8 together?
options: God is both the eternal keeper of truth and compassionate healer
questions.correctAnswer: God is both the eternal keeper of truth and compassionate healer
questions.explanation: Verse 6 reveals God's eternal faithfulness to truth, while verse 8 shows His compassion in healing the blind and raising the bowed down, illustrating a God who is both truthful and merciful.

questions.question: How does Psalms 146:4 contribute to our understanding of the doctrine of the soul and human existence?
options: It shows that human life and thoughts cease with death, underscoring human dependence on God
It teaches that the soul is immortal and independent from the body
It suggests humans become gods after death
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that human life and thoughts cease with death, underscoring human dependence on God
questions.explanation: Psalms 146:4 stresses that when a man dies, his breath departs and thoughts perish that day, highlighting the mortal nature of humanity and the need for divine help.

questions.question: What narrative arc connecting Psalms 146:1-2 and 146:10 can be drawn about praise and God's eternal kingship?
options: The Psalmist commits to lifelong praise because God reigns forever
Praise is unnecessary because God is silent
Praise is only for earthly kings
God's reign is temporary, so praise is limited
questions.correctAnswer: The Psalmist commits to lifelong praise because God reigns forever
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 express the Psalmist's intent to praise God all his life, culminating in verse 10's declaration of God's eternal reign, linking worship to the everlasting nature of God's kingship.

questions.question: Which doctrine is emphasized by the statement in Psalms 146:9 that 'the way of the wicked he turneth upside down'?
options: The wicked will inherit the earth
questions.explanation: This verse teaches the doctrine of God's sovereign judgment, showing that God actively opposes and overturns the plans of the wicked.
